title: Edge cases for the paper digest renderer

digest.abstract:
We study sparse attention with cost $O(n \log n)$ in the sequence length $n$, against $O(n^2)$ for dense attention. Training costs under \$5 per run and about $3 per GPU-hour on rented hardware.

On five benchmarks the method matches dense attention within $0.4$ points while using $\frac{1}{8}$ of the memory; the gap closes as $L \to \infty$.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Dense attention gets too slow on long inputs, so the authors replace it with a sparse pattern that keeps most of the accuracy.
sections.body:
Transformers compare every token with every other token, so cost grows with the square of the input length $n$. The authors keep a small set of **anchor tokens** that every token attends to, plus a local window.

- The anchors carry global context.
- The window carries local detail.

Together these give cost $O(n \log n)$.

sections.heading: Method
sections.headline: Each token looks at a fixed local window plus a few learned anchor tokens.
sections.body:
For a query $q_i$ the attention weights are

$$a_{ij} = \frac{\exp(q_i^\top k_j / \sqrt{d})}{\sum_{j' \in \mathcal{N}(i)} \exp(q_i^\top k_{j'} / \sqrt{d})},$$

where $\mathcal{N}(i)$ is the window around $i$ joined with the anchor set $\mathcal{A}$, with $|\mathcal{A}| = 64$.

sections.heading: Scaling to $10^6$ tokens
sections.headline: On five long-text benchmarks the sparse model scores within half a point of dense attention while using an eighth of the memory, and the result holds when the same comparison is repeated at four model sizes.
sections.body: Accuracy stays within $0.4$ points of the dense baseline on all five benchmarks. Memory falls to $\frac{1}{8}$ at $n = 65{,}536$. The authors scale inputs to $10^6$ tokens, where dense attention runs out of memory.

sections.heading: Limitations
sections.headline: The anchors are fixed after training, so very different inputs may need new ones.
sections.body: The anchor set is learned once and then frozen. The authors did not test inputs from domains far from the training data.

sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix gives the training settings and an ablation over the number of anchors.
sections.body: Training used a learning rate of $3 \times 10^{-4}$ with cosine decay. Fewer than $16$ anchors lose about two points; more than $64$ give no gain.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Memory use $M(n) = c_0 + c_1 n \log n$ for $n \in \{2^{10}, 2^{12}, \dots, 2^{20}\}$, fitted with $\hat{c}_1 = 1.7 \times 10^{-3}$ (dashed) against the dense curve $M_{\text{dense}}(n) = c_0 + c_2 n^2$ (solid); shaded bands are $\pm 1\sigma$ over $5$ seeds. Values above $80\,\text{GB}$ are out of memory on a single accelerator and are drawn as crosses. The run named sparse_attention_anchor64_window512_cosine_seed4 diverged and is omitted. Data and plotting code: https://example.org/a/very/long/path/that/must/wrap/inside/the/card/without/overflowing/at/375px.

We fit $c_1$ by least squares on the points in Figure 4.
